.. class:: warningmark
**Check the FAIRe workbook before you submit anything.** However the workbook was made (by hand, with FAIRe-ator, or with the FAIRe mapper tools), a person who knows the data should check it, and apply mapping's log if it made the workbook, before what this tool writes goes to a repository. Run FAIRe-fier on the workbook first. Submissions become public, and are hard to change once accepted.

param.name: input_file
param.label: FAIRe metadata workbook
param.help: Excel workbook with projectMetadata, sampleMetadata and experimentRunMetadata sheets, for example a FAIRe-ator template filled in with your data. Field names must be on row 3 of the sample and run sheets. Both the FAIRe layout (assay1, assay2 ... columns, as FAIRe-ator writes) and the FAIRe-NOAA layout are accepted.

param.name: organism_select
param.label: Organism for samples with none in the workbook
param.help: NCBI records environmental samples under a metagenome name. FAIRe has no organism field, so workbooks made by FAIRe-ator leave it out. Values already in an organism column are kept.

param.name: organism_name
param.label: Organism name
param.help: A scientific name from NCBI Taxonomy, for example 'lake water metagenome'. Search at https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/taxonomy

validator.message: Use letters, digits, spaces, '.', '-' and '_' only

param.name: runs_values
param.label: @FIELD@ values
param.help: Comma-separated, as written in experimentRunMetadata, for example @EXAMPLE@

validator.message: Enter one or more values separated by commas

**Workbook layout**
FAIRe2NCBI was written for the FAIRe-NOAA layout, where each assay has a projectMetadata column named after it. Workbooks from FAIRe-ator use columns called assay1, assay2 ... (or project_level for a single assay). The tool relabels those columns by their assay_name first, so both layouts work. The log records what was relabelled.

-----
**Rerunning outside Galaxy**
The **config** output holds every answer the tool gave to FAIRe2NCBI's questions. Run the upstream script with ``--config_file`` and the same answers are used. The comments at the top of the file list the changes the tool made to a copy of the workbook first; make the same changes for a local run to give the same result.
-----
**Credits**
This tool runs `FAIRe2NCBI <https://github.com/aomlomics/FAIRe2NCBI>`_ (CC0) from NOAA 'Omics, AOML, through a small Galaxy driver that answers its questions from the form and checks the result. The FAIRe checklist is described in Takahashi et al. (2025) *Environmental DNA* 7: e70100. The Galaxy tool was written by Oliver Berry (CSIRO), with Claude (Anthropic).
